$comment: Providers are interchangeable. A pay-per-use gateway is the Red Team's setup, not a requirement — subscription CLIs (type 'cli') and Anthropic-compatible adapters reach the same models without metered billing. Model specs are 'provider:model'; a bare model id uses defaultProvider.
$comment_concurrency: Kimi Code allows ~30 concurrent requests and 300-1200 per 5h window depending on tier. CLI providers spawn a subprocess each, so keep this low locally.

kimi-cli.$comment: Kimi Code CLI on a Kimi membership: npm i -g @kimi-code/cli, then `kimi` once to log in. No API key, no per-token cost. K3 needs Moderato tier or above.

claude-cli.$comment: Claude Code on a Claude subscription. Same idea, different seat.

codex-cli.$comment: OpenAI Codex CLI on a Codex/ChatGPT subscription. Same idea as kimi-cli/claude-cli: no per-token bills, needs the binary on PATH and an active login. --skip-git-repo-check lets it run in any checkout (CI has no per-path trust config); -s read-only keeps it from writing to or executing in the checked-out tree.

moonshot.$comment: Moonshot's Anthropic-compatible adapter. Metered, but no gateway in between.

zen.$comment: OpenCode Zen — the Red Team's own setup: one key, many models, pay-per-use.

ollama.$comment: Local Ollama OpenAI-compatible endpoint for the manual repro lab (security/lab). Not used by CI. Set OLLAMA_API_KEY to any non-empty string (Ollama ignores auth); lab/run.mjs defaults it to 'ollama' when unset.

hunt.$comment: Second channel, not the main one. Semgrep and OSV cover parser and supply-chain better; what stays here is the class no static rule can express — a fallback that silently lowers a guarantee.

verify.$comment: k-of-n refutation. A finding survives only if fewer than refuteThreshold refuters break it. The harness never lets a model refute its own finding.

report.$comment: Deliberately a different model than the one that found the bug. Final judge is the same primary-triage model (GPT) per issue #7 — deliberately NOT the model that ran verify, to avoid the judge grading its own refutation.

gate.$comment: Severities that turn the check red, after verification. blockOnTruncatedDiff: oversized diffs fail closed instead of reviewing only a prefix.

triage.$comment: Stage 2 — filter over scanner output. Use the strongest model available: agentic triage helps little with weak backbones. Primary triage model per issue #7: GPT reasons first, Claude refutes in the verify stage below — kept as two different backbones on purpose.
